quick_facts.label: What the job is
quick_facts.value: Semiconductor processing technicians carry out steps in the manufacture of electronic semiconductors, such as cleaning and polishing wafers and loading them into furnaces, chemical baths and circuit-forming equipment.

quick_facts.label: Other names for it
quick_facts.value: Job titles O*NET reports for this occupation (Semiconductor Processing Technicians) include Process Technician, Manufacturing Technician, Semiconductor Laboratory Technician and Diffusion Operator.

quick_facts.label: Typical preparation
quick_facts.value: O*NET places this occupation in Job Zone 1-2 (very little to some preparation needed): it usually requires a high school diploma or GED, though some occupations may not.

sections.heading: What a semiconductor process technician does
paragraphs: Semiconductor processing technicians carry out steps in the manufacture of electronic semiconductors, such as cleaning and polishing wafers and loading them into furnaces, chemical baths and circuit-forming equipment.

The tasks below are taken from the O*NET profile for Semiconductor Processing Technicians. O*NET is the US Department of Labor's occupation database, so this describes the job as it is profiled in the United States; titles and duties in Indian companies can differ.
bullets: Inspect materials and components for surface defects and measure circuitry with electronic test equipment.
Study work orders and processing charts to find the specifications and sequence of operations.
Clean semiconductor wafers using chemical baths or automatic wafer cleaners.
Keep processing, production and inspection records.

sections.heading: How people get into this job
paragraphs: O*NET places this occupation in Job Zone 1-2 (very little to some preparation needed): it usually requires a high school diploma or GED, though some occupations may not.
O*NET is the US Department of Labor's occupation database, so this describes the job as it is profiled in the United States; titles and duties in Indian companies can differ.
bullets: Common routes into this job on the Career Tree map: Polytechnic Diploma (Engineering); ITI (Industrial Training Institute).
Less common routes on the map: B.Sc (Bachelor of Science).
